nodes.plan: (root)

We merged the pipeline by sequentially chaining the domain-aware feature engineering, the TabularResNet model architecture, and the leak-free training and evaluation loop into a unified workflow. All shared variables, data transformations, and model components connect directly in memory while maintaining strict split isolation, standard scaling on the training split, and early stopping on hold-out classification accuracy. The final stage restores the best model weights, runs batch inference on test features, formats predictions to boolean format, and outputs the final validation metric.

nodes.code_summary: The pipeline performs domain-specific feature engineering (passenger ID group parsing, surname extraction, CryoSleep and zero-spend physical deduction, and cabin deck/side splitting) followed by log transformations and categorical ordinal encoding. Numerical inputs are normalized using StandardScaler fitted on training folds. The architecture is a Tabular Residual Network (TabularResNet) with LayerNorm, SiLU activations, and dropout, trained via AdamW with Cosine Annealing and early stopping on a Stratified K-Fold hold-out split.

nodes.plan: We merged the end-to-end pipeline into a unified script that executes domain feature engineering, categorical and numerical transformations fitted strictly on the training split, and the FT-Transformer neural architecture. The pipeline trains the model using BCE loss with cosine annealing and early stopping on hold-out validation accuracy, restores the best checkpoint weights, and performs batch inference on test samples to generate the final submission file.

nodes.code_summary: The pipeline implements an FT-Transformer (Feature Tokenizer Transformer) for tabular classification on the Spaceship Titanic dataset. Data preprocessing and feature engineering extract group dynamics, family size, deck/side interactions, expenditure aggregates, and log/ratio transformations with domain-specific zero-spending imputation. Categorical variables are encoded with OrdinalEncoder and continuous variables are scaled via StandardScaler, both fit strictly on the 80/20 train split. The model tokenizes categoricals via learned embeddings and continuous features using learnable Periodic Fourier Embeddings before passing tokens through a Pre-LN Transformer encoder and pooling head. Optimization uses AdamW with Cosine Annealing, label smoothing, gradient clipping, and early stopping.

nodes.code_summary: The implementation leverages domain-specific heuristics and passenger grouping to impute values (CryoSleep, HomePlanet, Cabin info), extracts spending ratios and log1p transforms, and standardizes continuous numerical features while encoding categorical features with entity embeddings. A custom TabularResNet architecture combining continuous feature projections, categorical embeddings, residual blocks with LayerNorm/Dropout/SiLU, and label smoothing loss is trained with AdamW and cosine annealing. Validation is performed using fold 0 of a 5-fold Stratified K-Fold setup, tracking accuracy with early stopping.

nodes.code_summary:
1. Preprocessing & Feature Engineering: Performed domain-specific physical invariant deductions (e.g. CryoSleep, amenity spending, Cabin deck constraints), group and surname aggregations, log1p amenity spends, cabin spatial metrics, and out-of-fold smoothed Bayesian target encoding.
2. Validation Strategy: Stratified 5-fold split with Fold 0 held out as the final evaluation set and the remaining folds split internally using 4-fold StratifiedKFold.
3. Model Architecture: Ensemble composed of LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, and a custom PyTorch TabularMLP with entity embeddings for categorical features.
4. Blending & Inference: Optimized log-loss weights via SLSQP convex simplex optimization over out-of-fold predictions, tuned classification threshold on the hold-out validation set, and output predictions for the test set.

nodes.code_summary: The pipeline implements domain-specific tabular feature engineering (group parsing, cabin decomposition, expenditure indicators, and physical constraint resolution). Continuous variables are scaled with RobustScaler and categorical variables are encoded via OrdinalEncoder using a leak-free 5-fold Stratified split structure. nodes.plan: We merged the pipeline into a unified, leak-free workflow that performs domain-informed feature engineering and physical constraint imputation, instantiates the TabNet neural architecture with gated linear units and sparse attentive feature transformers, and executes an early-stopping training schedule. All data pre-processing, stateful imputations, and feature scalers are strictly isolated to the training split, and the best model weights based on holdout validation accuracy are restored to generate test predictions. nodes.code_summary: The code loads the Spaceship Titanic dataset and applies domain-specific feature engineering (amenity spending metrics, family/group extraction, cabin parsing, and logical deduplication of CryoSleep and HomePlanet). It defines an ensemble composed of LightGBM, XGBoost, and CatBoost with StratifiedKFold validation, alongside out-of-fold leave-one-out target encoding for group and cabin level signals, and optimizes a weighted blend with threshold tuning.

nodes.plan:
### Root Cause & Improvement Sketch

The error (`KeyError: 'Group_Target'`) occurred because the target-encoded features (`Group_Target`, `Has_Group_Target`, `Cabin_Target`, `Has_Cabin_Target`) were included in `feature_cols` and `num_cols`, but they had not yet been created when median imputation was performed on `processed_train`. To fix this, median imputation is restricted to the numerical columns currently present in the DataFrame, and the target-encoded features are explicitly pre-initialized on both train and test sets before cross-validation assignment. In addition, categorical features for XGBoost are cast via string representations before dictionary mapping to ensure safe and error-free numeric encoding across pandas versions.
